requirements.requirement: Establish PostgreSQL streaming replication with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as standbys
requirements.summary: node1 initialized with wal_level=replica and started; node2 and node3 were base-backed up from node1 with -R (standby.signal + primary_conninfo) and started. pg_stat_replication on node1 showed both walreceivers streaming, and both standbys returned pg_is_in_recovery=t with baseline rows replicated.

requirements.requirement: When the primary is lost, a standby takes over as writable primary without losing committed data
requirements.summary: A row was committed on node1 and confirmed replicated to node2 (cmd-f21139918f9e4b54, cmd-26a4e52544344232) before node1's postgres was stopped to simulate primary loss (cmd-4c978900544d4b88, exit code 2 reflects pg_isready reporting down, expected). node2 was promoted via pg_ctl promote and confirmed pg_is_in_recovery=false (cmd-24f74b9f09474065), then accepted a new write while retaining all prior committed rows including the pre-failover one (cmd-1206359038d645a1).

requirements.requirement: The other standby and the recovered former primary follow whichever system is primary after failover
requirements.summary: node3's primary_conninfo was repointed to node2 and restarted; it confirmed pg_is_in_recovery=true and showed post-failover data present (cmd-8f397ac3a8544ba0, cmd-aba2f5d7a26e4c21), and node2's pg_stat_replication showed node3 streaming (cmd-c27acfac1ca94a43). node1 was rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2, started as a standby with pg_is_in_recovery=true and all data intact (cmd-f124817205164c97, cmd-dcd70e948eb14438), and node2 confirmed both node1 and node3 streaming (cmd-fcadb62c4fb24289).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: streaming replication was established with node1 as primary and node2/node3 as standbys; a bounded failover drill showed node2 promoted to writable primary with zero loss of a previously committed row and acceptance of new writes; node3 was repointed to the new primary and node1 was rebuilt and rejoined as a standby, both confirmed streaming from node2. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also executed and verified for all three nodes, showing pre-restart boot identity and healthy state, a restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot identity, and full recovery of postgres role, replication streaming, and all ledger data — this is fully consistent with the fixed before/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations were found; the only residue (a per-node /tmp/reboot.log) is a low-risk artifact of the reboot mechanism itself.
limitations: The after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare was disabled/static), so no separate preparer-caused state could be distinguished from executor changes; all executor-comparison diffs are attributed directly to the executor's actions, which is consistent with the timeline.

Command exit code 2 on cmd-4c978900544d4b88 (pg_isready after stopping postgres) and return_code 3 on early os-release/hostname probes are expected discovery/verification outcomes, not task failures, and were treated as such.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing command traces to a clear purpose: package installation, initdb/config for the primary, pg_basebackup for standbys, the deliberate failover drill (stop/promote/repoint/rejoin), rc-update persistence for reboot survival, and the mandatory reboot protocol on each node. No unexplained troubleshooting mutations or abandoned experiments were found in the timeline. The reboot protocol left a small /tmp/reboot.log file on each node (visible in after-executor temporary-files diff for node1, node2, node3) — a low-risk, bounded residue directly caused by the nohup-backgrounded reboot mechanism used to satisfy the mandatory restart protocol, not an unnecessary mutation. Package-health 'chrony.drift' entries are identical before and after and are pre-existing, unrelated to the executor. No unsafe exposure, weakened security controls, or damaged package state was observed; listening-socket diffs show only the expected addition of postgres on 5432 and normal post-reboot ephemeral changes (sshd PID, DHCP lease renewal).
